title: Is Space-Time Attention All You Need for Video Understanding?
grouping: A 3 x 5 grid without frames: columns are five attention schemes, rows are three consecutive frames labelled at the left with rotated text (frame t - delta, frame t, frame t + delta). Each cell is one video frame cut into a 4 x 4 grid of patches separated by white gutters. Column names sit under the grid with the scheme's short code in brackets, its letters coloured.
shapes_depth: Photographic patches only, no boxes or arrows. The query patch is tinted blue in the middle frame of every column; the patches it attends to are tinted with translucent colour washes - red for space or joint space-time, green for the time-only step, yellow and magenta for local and global, green, yellow and magenta for time, width and height. Untinted patches stay in their natural colours.
proposed_highlight: No scheme is singled out by drawing; the coloured letters in each column label (e.g. T in green, S in red) act as the legend for the tint colours in that column.
lesson: Explain attention variants with a grid of real frames: columns = variants, rows = three consecutive frames cut into patches, the query patch in blue and each attended set in a translucent tint whose colour matches the coloured letter in the column label.
notes: Venue ICML from arXiv journal_ref/comment as reported by refs search (arXiv fallback). Name 'TimeSformer' from the paper's own captions. The paper's Fig. 1 draws the same five schemes as block diagrams; this figure shows them as data. Annotation note (2026-11-15): Not a pipeline/architecture figure: it visualises attention patterns over video patches (a concept comparison), so it is a reference for parallel-panel comparisons rather than a method skeleton.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: five identical panels side by side, one per self-attention scheme (Space, Joint Space-Time, Divided Space-Time, Sparse Local Global, Axial), each the same three video frames cut into 4x4 patches with the same blue query patch and the attended patches tinted by colour

relations.form: five equal columns on one row with aligned frame rows, captioned beneath with the scheme name and its colour-coded letters (S, ST, T+S, L+G, T+W+H)

each scheme is drawn directly on real video frames (a hand and a bottle) split into a patch grid, the query patch tinted blue in frame t and the patches it attends to washed in colour across frames t-delta, t and t+delta
frames stack top to bottom (frame t-delta, frame t, frame t+delta) with the row labels written once at the far left

channels.colour: tint = which attention step covers a patch, keyed by the coloured letters in each caption (red S/ST, green T, yellow L or W, magenta G or H); blue = the query patch, unkeyed; yellow and magenta carry different meanings in the Sparse Local Global and Axial panels
channels.shape: square image patches only; no module shapes are drawn
channels.frame: white gaps separate patches and frames; panels are separated only by spacing

quality.strengths: the compared designs are drawn as identical panels on the same frames and the same query, so the difference between schemes is only which patches are tinted - a reader sees at a glance that joint attention covers everything while divided attention covers one row of time plus one frame; the caption letters double as the colour key, so no separate legend is needed
quality.weaknesses: yellow and magenta change meaning between the last two panels (local/global vs width/height), and the blue query patch is not keyed; the proposed Divided Space-Time scheme sits in the middle with no emphasis, so the paper's choice does not stand out; the red wash over whole frames in the Space and Joint panels hides the image content it covers

insights.structure: Five identical columns, one per attention scheme (Space, Joint Space-Time, Divided Space-Time, Sparse Local Global, Axial), each a vertical stack of three frames (t-delta, t, t+delta) cut into 4x4 patch grids.
insights.data: Frames are real video frames split into patches with white gutters; one query patch is blue and the patches it attends to are tinted with translucent colour overlays.
insights.emphasis: Colour encodes attention type and is echoed in the column caption letters (S red, T green, L yellow, G magenta, W/H), so each caption doubles as a legend.
insights.flow: Read column by column left to right comparing schemes; within a column top to bottom across time; no arrows at all.
insights.avoid: Overlapping translucent tints (red over patches, yellow over magenta) make some attended regions hard to tell apart, and the blue query patch is small.

arrangement.units: five unframed columns of identical frame stacks, each captioned underneath
arrangement.inputs_as: real video frames tiled into patches
arrangement.shared: row labels frame t-delta / t / t+delta at the left apply to all columns
